summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — BESI.AS +10%, STMPA.PA +7%, ASM.AS +5%, ANTO.L +5%, IFX.DE +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (HSBA.L -6%, RKT.L -5%, MBG.DE -4%, BP.L -3%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: BESI.AS (+10.44%) — No same-day source found. Likely a rebound in AI-packaging semis after Besi's strong Q3 (reported orders ~€343M, ~15% above consensus), but I couldn't confirm that as the driver on 10-28. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: BESI.AS is an Amsterdam-listed mid-cap semicap equipment name, probably below the cap/liquidity cutoffs. A gap-up on news is also hard for a post-open momentum filter to enter, and RSI or gap caps likely excluded it.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BESI.AS is an Amsterdam-listed mid-cap semicap equipment name, probably below the cap/liquidity cutoffs. A gap-up on news is also hard for a post-open momentum filter to enter, and RSI or gap caps likely excluded it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a small-allocation 'EU semicap/AI-supply-chain' watchlist (BESI, ASMI, ASML) to the momentum universe, and let it bypass the gap-size cap when volume is ≥2x the 20-day average and a sector peer is also up.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver found. My search returned no Oct 28, 2026 coverage of STMicro. The +6.6% is plausibly a post-Q3-results rerating or a European semiconductor sector rally, but I couldn't verify either.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: STMPA.PA is a large-cap Euronext Paris semiconductor, and no strategy lists it. If the move was earnings-driven, the gap-up would also have been priced at the open, ahead of any post-signal entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add liquid Euronext Paris/Milan large caps like STMPA.PA to the momentum universe, with a gap-up rule (e.g. open gap ≥ +4% on ≥1.5× average volume) that allows entry after the first 30 minutes.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 2026 results beat on revenue with adjusted operating margin up to 33.4%, and a higher outlook. ASM also announced a new €300M buyback after finishing its €150M program.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ASM.AS is a ~€35-40B Dutch semiconductor-equipment large cap that no strategy lists. It was also an earnings-gap move, so the pre-open reaction would have beaten any post-open momentum signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a Euronext Amsterdam semicap watchlist (ASM.AS, BESI.AS, ASML.AS) to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings gate release names with a post-results gap ≥ +3% within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-28. Searches turned up no company RNS or Antofagasta-specific news for the day, so the +5.06% is most likely a copper or sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ANTO.L is a FTSE 100 copper miner, a large-cap commodity name that no strategy's universe includes. With no stock-specific news, a news-reactive bot would not have triggered either.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'LSE miners / copper' basket (ANTO.L, GLEN.L, RIO.L) to the momentum-trader universe, gated on a copper-futures move of at least +2% (the threshold is a placeholder), so sector-driven days like this one are caught.

top_movers.catalyst: No dated news found for IFX.DE today; the +3.8% looks like a sector-wide semiconductor/AI-linked rally, possibly after peer results. Not confirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: IFX.DE is a large-cap German (Xetra) semiconductor, and no strategy lists it. With no company-specific catalyst, a news-reactive filter would also have had nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU semis (IFX.DE, STM.PA, ASML.AS) to the momentum-trader universe, or add a sector-basket trigger that admits peers when ≥3 semis gain ≥3% on the same day.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. BTRW.L (Barratt Redrow, UK housebuilder) rose 3.8% with only routine buyback notices in the news, so this is likely a UK housebuilder or rates/gilt-yield sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BTRW.L is a UK mid-cap housebuilder, and no strategy's universe includes it. With no company-specific catalyst, a news-reactive bot had nothing to trigger on, and a +3.8% sector-beta move is a modest signal for momentum filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add UK housebuilders (BTRW.L, PSN.L, TW.L) to the momentum universe with a sector-relative-strength rule, e.g. enter when the name is up ≥3% and its sector basket is up ≥2% on above-average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: HSBC Q3 results missed consensus: net interest income fell about $2.6B short of estimates and EPS and revenue were below forecasts. A $1B buyback and a 32% rise in pre-tax profit didn't offset it, and CET1 slipped to 13.9%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HSBA.L is a large-cap UK/HK bank that no strategy covers. The drop was also a gap-down on a results release before the open, so post-open momentum signals would arrive late. The bot is long-only, so it couldn't short the move. top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 financials (HSBA.L, BARC.L, LLOY.L) to the mean-reversion universe, with an earnings-gap entry rule: gap ≤ -5% and RSI(14) < 30 on a fundamentals-driven miss, size-capped at 50% of a normal position.

top_movers.catalyst: Reckitt (RKT.L) Q3 update: Core LFL revenue +3.3% vs 3.6% expected. FY26 LFL growth guidance cut to 3.5-4.5% from 4-5% on Lysol supply problems, weak China VMS and a softer cold/flu season.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: RKT.L is a large-cap UK consumer-staples name that no strategy lists. It was also a scheduled-results gap-down, and a long-only bot gets no entry from a drop like that.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a long-only 'post-earnings guidance-cut' watchlist covering FTSE 100 staples. Flag names that gap down ≥4% on results, then re-enter only after RSI(14)<30 and 2 days of stabilising closes, instead of trying to trade the gap.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely follow-through selling after Mercedes-Benz's weak Q3 2026 report: Cars margin about 2.5%, China sales down 31%, and a cut to the Cars return-on-sales target. Exact report date and cause unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MBG.DE is a large-cap German auto name that no strategy covers. The drop also came from a known earnings and China-weakness story, so pre-market positioning would have beaten any post-move signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap Xetra/DAX autos to the mean-reversion or news-reactive universe, with an earnings-window gate that blocks new entries within 2 trading days of results and releases after a gap of -3% or more.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-28 — likely an oil-price-driven sector move, with BP sliding alongside crude and the energy majors amid Iran-related geopolitical swings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BP.L is a UK FTSE 100 large-cap integrated oil major and apparently isn't in any strategy's ticker list. A sector-beta move with no stock-specific catalyst also gives little signal to a news-reactive bot.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a uk-eu energy-majors basket (BP.L, SHEL.L) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a Brent daily move beyond ±2.5%, so oil-driven sector drops are captured without needing stock-specific news.
